title: Floodgate Relay
description: This game is a movement-based hydraulic routing puzzle set inside a compact canal-control facility. You move a caretaker avatar through a network of walkways, valve stations, and sluice controls while water continuously enters the system from one or more source channels. The main interaction is that stepping on or activating a control changes the local water routing: some controls open or close gates, some flip a channel diverter, and some temporarily drain or reserve water in a holding tank. Water then visibly fills connected chambers, powers wheels, raises floats, or spills into drains depending on the current gate layout, so the challenge is to sequence your route through the control room in the right order to make the right parts of the canal network active at the same time. The level contains several target basins or mechanisms that each require a specific water state: for example, one chamber may need to be filled, another must stay empty, and another may need flowing water rather than stored water. When the hydraulic layout satisfies one of those targets, its mechanism visibly locks into the solved state, and to finish the level you must satisfy all required basin or mechanism conditions simultaneously or in a required order depending on the layout. Movement and waiting both matter because the water state evolves only after actions, and every action also advances a pressure meter or storm timer shown on the HUD. If the timer runs out, or if too much water spills into marked overflow channels, the facility fails and the level resets. Overall, it is a timed systems-routing puzzle: you explore a water network, manipulate gates and junctions, reason about how local controls propagate through the larger canal layout, and try to put the whole facility into the required hydraulic configuration before time or overflow defeats you.

title: Magnet Crane Yard
description: This game is a grid-based logistics puzzle where you control a magnetic crane moving along fixed overhead rails above a cluttered cargo yard. The crane can move between rail junctions, lower or raise its magnet, and switch its polarity or attachment mode, and the key mechanic is that different cargo blocks react differently to the crane depending on their material and orientation. Some crates can be lifted directly, some can only be dragged along metal tracks, some repel each other when brought too close under the wrong polarity, and some act as blockers that must be parked temporarily in staging bays before the real target pieces can be delivered. Each level contains a small set of delivery docks that expect specific cargo modules, shown visually by the silhouette and marking of the dock itself. When the correct cargo is lowered into the matching dock, that dock locks in and becomes solved. To clear the level, you have to place every required cargo piece into its correct destination without jamming the yard into an unsalvageable layout. Every crane action consumes battery charge, represented by an energy bar, and some inefficient moves also generate heat in the magnet system, so the challenge is not only figuring out what goes where but also sequencing pickups, temporary parking, and route access efficiently enough to finish before the power budget is exhausted. If the battery runs out, or if you leave the crane in an overheated state for too long, the whole yard resets to its initial configuration. Overall, it is a timed manipulation-and-ordering puzzle: you control a single overhead machine, rearrange an interdependent set of cargo objects with polarity-sensitive interactions, and try to deliver all required modules in the right order before energy and congestion beat you.

title: Bell Tower Synchrony
description: This game is a click-based timing and signal-routing puzzle played on a board of visible bell mechanisms, relays, and wire channels. Every clickable module belongs to a small family of signal devices, and the main interaction is that clicking a device changes how it handles pulses: a click might rotate a switch junction, advance a relay’s delay by one step, toggle whether a gate passes or blocks a pulse, or arm a repeater that re-emits a signal on the next beat. After each click, the system advances by one global clock tick, and bright pulse markers travel visibly through the network so the player can see exactly how the circuit responds over time. The level contains several bell towers or receiver nodes that must ring under specific conditions, such as receiving a pulse on the same beat, receiving pulses in a required order, or being hit while a local phase indicator is aligned. These requirements are communicated visually by the receiver framing and nearby preview indicators rather than text. A receiver visibly locks when its timing condition is satisfied, and the level is solved only when all receiver nodes have been triggered correctly within the same overall attempt. Every click consumes one unit from a countdown bar, so the challenge is to understand how to reshape the pulse network with a small number of edits and then sequence those edits so the moving signals arrive where they need to go at the right times. If the move budget reaches zero before all receivers are satisfied, the bell network powers down and the level resets. Overall, it is a timed temporal-logic puzzle: you modify a living signal circuit, watch pulses propagate through delays and switches, and try to synchronize several local timing constraints before the move budget runs out.
